title: Exact solution of the two-dimensional one-component plasma on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere
abstract: arXiv:2611.21652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve exactly the two-dimensional one-component plasma at coupling $\Gamma=2$ on the truncated Beltrami pseudosphere, a surface of constant negative curvature bounded by two parallels. A conformal map onto a flat cylinder leaves the particles interacting through the flat-cylinder potential, with the curvature entering only through the area element. The partition function becomes a product of incomplete gamma functions, the density is explicit, and all correlations are determinantal. Since the area is bounded, the large-N limit is taken at fixed shape. The free energy, obtained through the constant term with every coefficient in closed form, contains a bulk term (1/2)N ln N, a term linear in N, the flat hard-wall surface tension times the total boundary length, and a shape-dependent constant, with no ln N term. This is the conformal-anomaly prediction for Euler characteristic zero, tested here on a surface where the integrated Gaussian and boundary curvatures are separately nonzero and cancel. The expansion coincides term by term with the cylinder result of Shen and Forrester, whose universal constants are quadratures of the two boundary layers. At both walls the density tends to the flat contact value $n_b$ ln 2, from opposite sides, although the circumferences differ by a factor cosh u_max. We compare the asymptotics with the exact solution up to N=4096, and Monte Carlo simulations at $\Gamma= $1, 4 and 6, validated against the exact $\Gamma= $ 2 density, show how the boundary layers evolve with coupling.
summary:
- Exact Γ=2 solution on truncated Beltrami pseudosphere via conformal map to a flat cylinder; partition function is a product of incomplete gamma functions and all correlations are determinantal.
- Free energy contains a bulk (½ N ln N), linear‑N, surface‑tension (∝ boundary length) and a shape‑dependent constant, matching the conformal‑anomaly prediction for Euler characteristic zero.
- Boundary density approaches the flat contact value \(n_b\ln 2\); analytic results agree with cylinder limits and Monte‑Carlo data for Γ = 1,

title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
authors: Omar Pedraza, Erik D\'iaz-Bautista, L. A. L\'opez, Daniel O-Campa
abstract: arXiv:2611.21675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.
summary:
- q‑deformed Dirac‑oscillator spectra and eigenfunctions for monolayer/bilayer graphene in a magnetic field, recovering Landau levels as q→
- Explicit construction of bilayer lowest Landau levels and q‑dependent probability current densities.
- Partition functions via zeta‑function/Euler‑Maclaurin yield distinct thermodynamic responses for monolayer vs. bilayer, revealing q‑deformation effects.

title: Renormalization-Group Foundation of Critical Modes in Correlation Matrices
authors: Yanhua Zhang, Mingmei Xu, Jinghua Fu, Yuanfang Wu
abstract: arXiv:2611.21676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Based on the relevant scaling operators of renormalization-group theory, we establish a theoretical framework for constructing complete families of critical-sensitive fluctuation observables and their connected correlation matrices. The corresponding eigenstates of the correlation matrices reveal a hierarchy of multiscale critical correlation patterns and the leading normalized eigenvalues and their ratios show the finite-size scaling behavior. Applying this framework to the two-dimensional Ising model, the correlation matrices associated with both spin and energy operators are constructed. The resulting energy-sector eigenstate patterns, together with the scaling behavior of the leading eigenvalues, provide further support for the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss its potential extension to systems with unknown Hamiltonians.
summary:
- Uses RG scaling operators to construct complete families of critical‑sensitive fluctuation observables and their correlation matrices.
- Eigenstates reveal a multiscale hierarchy of critical correlations; leading eigenvalues and ratios obey finite‑size scaling.
- Applied to 2D Ising: spin and energy matrices reproduce expected patterns, supporting the framework and hinting at use for unknown Hamiltonians.

title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
abstract: arXiv:2611.21697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of {8, 3} and {12, 3} lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous {\pi} flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.
summary:
- Constructed and solved the Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions via finite quotients of triangle groups.
- Determined ground‑state superselection sectors, flux backgrounds, and degeneracies governed by lattice symmetries at the isotropic point.
- Found a non‑monotonic two‑vison gap and algebraic decay of matter‑fermion correlations even for modest system sizes.

title: Probing Phase Fluctuations in Cuprates by Multidimensional Josephson Spectroscopy
authors: Albert Liu, Danica Pavicevic, Alex G\'omez Salvador, Marios H. Michael, Michael Fechner, Pedro M. Lozano, Qiang Li, Genda D. Gu, Eugene Demler, Andrea Cavalleri
abstract: arXiv:2611.21708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.
summary:
- Angle‑resolved multidimensional THz spectroscopy shows a crossover near Tc in La₁.₈₃Sr₀.₁₇CuO₄ from mean‑field to fluctuation‑dominated third‑order Josephson nonlinearity.
- The non‑rephasing multidimensional signal uniquely probes short‑range superconducting phase fluctuations above Tc.
- A theoretical framework connects the out‑of‑plane optical response to both mean‑field and fluctuation regimes, supporting the pre‑formed pair hypothesis.

title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
authors: Salvatore D. Pace, Sakura Schafer-Nameki, Carolyn Zhang
abstract: arXiv:2611.21715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.
summary:
- SymTFT encodes ordinary and generalized symmetries in a higher‑dimensional topological theory, separating symmetry data from system details.
- In (1+d fusion‑category symmetries, it classifies anomalies, gapped phases, and organizes gapless phase symmetry structures.
- The review extends the framework to higher dimensions, continuous, fermionic, mixed‑state, and spacetime symmetries.

title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
abstract: arXiv:2611.21720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $\rho$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $\rho$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $\rho -1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.
summary:
- Extends Luttinger theorem to fractionalized Fermi liquids (FL*) showing Fermi‑surface volume shifts by a quantized amount (e.g., ρ → ρ − .
- Connects the shift to symmetry‑fractionalization data of quantum spin liquids with spinon excitations.
- Generalizes Oshikawa’s flux‑insertion argument to FL* and discusses implications for gapless spin liquids.

title: Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moir\'e Systems
authors: Conor Smith, Yubo Yang, Shiwei Zhang, Miguel A. Morales
abstract: arXiv:2611.21745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moir\'e superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $\nu_B=1$ in the presence of a moir\'e superlattice potential, with three electrons per moir\'e cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moir\'e bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moir\'e minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a N\'eel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.
summary:
- Coexistence of molecular charge order and quantized Hall response in Moiré bilayers at ν_B=
- Phase diagram shows triangular potential → Wigner crystal; reduced potential → Hall conductance emerges while charge order persists.
- Honeycomb point yields doublon‑based Ising degrees of freedom with short‑range correlations.

title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
abstract: arXiv:2611.21773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $\rho_n=\sin^2\theta_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $\gamma$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.
summary:
- Hidden convexity of the condensation energy in the first quadrant yields existence and uniqueness (up to gauge) of the superconducting minimizer for any positive, non‑increasing power‑law interaction.
- The normal state is the unique minimizer above the critical temperature; a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations appears precisely when the normal state becomes linearly unstable.
- For temperature‑dependent families with pointwise continuity and uniform decay, the minimizing density varies continuously in weighted ℓ¹, confirming the thermodynamic conjectures for the γ‑model, Einstein phonons, and general spectra.

title: High-resolution top-down nanopatterning of NbN thin films for superconducting metamaterials
authors: Francesca Incalza, Davide Mondin, Dip Joti Paul, Matteo Castellani, Alejandro Simon, Rocco A. Vitalone, Dmitri N. Basov, Karl K. Berggren
abstract: arXiv:2611.21848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic nanopatterning offers a route to tailoring vortex motion and the electromagnetic response of superconducting films, providing a basis for superconducting metamaterials. Here, we report a high-resolution top-down nanopatterning process for ultrathin epitaxial NbN films on sapphire substrates. Electron-beam lithography using hydrogen silsesquioxane (HSQ) and ZEP 530A resists was optimized through proximity-effect correction and adhesion-layer integration. Dense superconducting nanowire grids with pitches down to 70 nm were fabricated, alongside millimeter-square areas patterned with 100-nm-pitch hole arrays with high pattern fidelity. A thin Si capping layer was found to significantly improve HSQ adhesion on epitaxial NbN. The nanopatterns were successfully transferred into 5-nm-thick NbN films by reactive ion etching (RIE). Structural and dimensional characterization was performed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM), enabling cross-validation of nanoscale feature dimensions and etch quality. Electrical transport measurements reveal periodic resistance minima and switching-current oscillations at magnetic fields set by the hole-array pitch, consistent with enhanced vortex pinning when the vortex configuration matches the patterned lattice. Cryogenic THz time-domain spectroscopy further reveals a reduced superfluid density in the nanopatterned region relative to pristine NbN, while both regions have a spectroscopic superconducting transition near 14 K. These results establish a robust fabrication platform for superconducting nanopatterns targeting vortex pinning, metamaterials, and quantum-device applications.
summary:
- Developed high‑resolution top‑down nanopatterning of 5 nm NbN films on sapphire, achieving 70 nm pitch nanowire grids and 100 nm pitch hole arrays via HSQ/ZEP resists with proximity‑effect correction.
- Introduced a thin Si capping layer to enhance HSQ adhesion; patterns transferred through RIE and validated by SEM, TEM, and AFM.
- Transport and cryogenic THz measurements reveal periodic resistance minima, switching‑current oscillations, and reduced superfluid density, evidencing enhanced vortex pinning and modified electromagnetic response.

title: Coexisting orders and dipolar Luttinger liquids in $\mathbb{Z}_N$ quantum torus chain
authors: Seunghun Lee, Seungho Lee, Hyun-Yong Lee, Jung Hoon Han
abstract: arXiv:2611.22046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a unified ground-state phase diagram for the one-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ quantum torus chain, which is connected to dipolar cluster and dipolar Ising chains via noninvertible dualities. Combining tensor-network calculations with bosonization and perturbation theory, we establish a rich phase diagram governed by the local Hilbert-space dimension $N$ and its parity. We identify phases with coexisting $X$ and $Z$ long-range orders ($C$ phase), and dipolar Luttinger liquids (dLL$_{\rm I}$ and dLL$_{\rm II}$) separating coexisting phases from single-order phases. Gapless dipolar excitations coexist with long-range order in dLLs. Both the $C$ and dLL phases appear at $N \geq 5$, but only the $C$ phases persist as $N\to \infty$. The stability of the dLL phase is understood by an emergent Luttinger liquid theory, with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions out of it driven by competing umklapp and clock anisotropy perturbations. For odd $N \geq 5$, a third dLL phase (dLL$_{\rm III}$) emerges near $\theta = \pi$ due to the low-energy dynamics inside the exponentially degenerate ground-state manifold that maps onto an effective XXZ chain. Duality considerations suggest a possible gapless dipolar symmetry-protected topological phase and spontaneous dipole-symmetry breaking in dipolar cluster chains.
summary:
- Unified phase diagram for 1D ℤ_N quantum torus chain, linked to dipolar cluster/Ising chains via noninvertible dualities.
- Coexisting X‑Z long‑range order (C phase) and dipolar Luttinger liquids (dLL_I, dLL_II, dLL_III) with gapless dipolar excitations, appearing for N ≥ 5 (and odd N ≥ 5 near θ = π).

title: Orbital differentiation in a rare earth ion near half filling
authors: D. W. Tam, {\O}. S. Fjellv{\aa}g, B. Gonano, E. X. M. Trewick, M. M{\aa}nsson
abstract: arXiv:2611.22462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the electronic structure of rare earth ions, details can be crucial for understanding the origin of correlated states. Currently, state-of-the-art wavefunction-based methods (e.g. CASSCF) can capture single-ion properties of molecular magnets and some band insulating systems, but are expensive to perform, and cannot be applied to metallic systems. Here, we carry out full multiplet calculations for SmN with the cubic rock-salt structure using the crystal field software Quanty. The calculated experimental observables from our model agree precisely with magnetic susceptibility and inelastic neutron scattering experiments, and the spatially resolved spin density also agrees with DFT predictions. By tuning the crystal field parameters, our full multiplet-derived wavefunctions reveal the presence of orbital differentiation of the ground $J=\frac{5}{2}$ manifold into two groups, which are distinct subspaces with different orbital stiffness. This violation of Hund's rule, observed with a fast and inexpensive calculation tool, represents a step forward for microscopic models of rare earth materials, and may provide support for the claim of unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.
summary:
- Full multiplet calculations with Quanty reproduce SmN’s magnetic susceptibility, neutron scattering, and spin density.
- Crystal‑field tuning shows orbital differentiation in the J = 5/2 ground state, splitting it into two subspaces with different orbital stiffness (Hund’s rule violation).
- Results aid microscopic modeling of rare‑earth systems and support possible unconventional triplet superconductivity in SmN.

title: Preformed excitons in the excitonic density-wave state of monolayer 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$
authors: Fei Yang, Keyu Wei, Dekun Yang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yong Zhang, Xuefeng Wang, Fucong Fei, Fengqi Song, Binghai Yan, Xiaoxiang Xi, Junwei Liu
abstract: arXiv:2611.22536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-incoherent preformed excitons have long been anticipated in excitonic insulators, yet their characteristic signatures and underlying physics remain elusive, as the electrical neutrality of excitons hinders direct probes of condensate phase coherence. Here we exploit the emergent excitonic density wave driven by phase-coherent pairings in systems hosting momentum-separated electron and hole Fermi pockets, such as monolayer 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$, as an experimentally accessible probe of excitonic phase coherence. We observe in 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$ that the density-wave order and its associated emergent collective excitations, as revealed by Raman spectroscopy, vanish above $T_c\approx80~$K, whereas the excitonic-insulator state, characterized by a single-particle gap in transport and tunneling measurements, persists up to $T_g\approx100~$K, revealing an intermediate pseudogap-like regime of preformed excitons without long-range phase coherence. Theoretically, we attribute this intriguing separation to two distinct processes governing the loss of excitonic order by its own emergent excitations: boson-driven phase decoherence and fermion-driven pair breaking. Specifically, we identify an emergent low-lying collective excitation as a lattice-pinned phason (phase mode), whose heating-induced gap softening enhances phase fluctuations and drives condensate phase decoherence above $T_c$, while thermal excitations of fermionic quasiparticles gradually suppress and ultimately destroy pairing amplitude at the higher $T_g$. The self-consistent microscopic calculation quantitatively captures our key observations, establishing an excitonic realization of preformed-pairing physics.
summary:
- Density‑wave order in monolayer 1T′‑MoTe₂ vanishes at Tc ≈ 80 K, while the excitonic gap survives to Tg ≈ 100 K, revealing a pseudogap of preformed excitons.
- Raman spectra detect a lattice‑pinned phason whose gap softens with temperature, driving phase decoherence above Tc.
- Theory attributes the two‑step loss of order to boson‑driven phase fluctuations (phason) and fermion‑driven pair breaking at higher T.

title: Domain walls of a spin-chirality ferroelectric as tunable quantum particles
authors: Aleksandr Buzdakov, Atharva Hingane, Sergey Artyukhin
abstract: arXiv:2611.22662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In frustrated spin chains with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange, the vector spin chirality sets the electric polarization, so a ferroelectric domain wall is a domain wall of the chirality. The semiclassical picture suggests nonlocal switching dynamics due to topological constraints on the spins, but little is known about such domain walls in a quantum spin chain. Using density-matrix renormalization group calculations for a frustrated spin-1/2 XXZ chain in which a bond alternation $\delta$ opens a spin gap, we show that the wall then becomes a quantum particle. In a finite chain, it has the energy levels and wave functions of a particle in a box, and it moves under an electric field as a particle under a constant force does. In the infinite chain, its mass grows by more than two orders of magnitude as $\delta$ decreases and diverges at $\delta^*\approx0.012$, where the bottom of its band becomes flat; below $\delta^*$ the band has two degenerate minima away from its center. The large mass results from a near cancellation of in-plane and out-of-plane exchange energies.

title: Structural Response to the Hidden Charge Order in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_7$
authors: Darren C. Peets, Nikita D. Andriushin, Tobias Ritschel, Morgan C. Allison, Nikolai S. Pavlovskii, Anton A. Kulbakov, Alexandre Ivanov, Jose R. Linares Mardegan, Pablo J. Bereciartua, Sonia Francoual, Jochen Geck, Dmytro S. Inosov
abstract: arXiv:2611.22864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We previously reported `hidden' charge order below $\sim$330 K in the centrosymmetric skyrmion host Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_7$ [J.-H. Kim et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 097203 (2021)], finally identifying the charge disproportionation and localization transition that had been first seen in the 1960s. We detected this through resonant x-ray scattering, which directly probes electron density, but is only indirectly sensitive to the lattice structure. This left open the question of whether the charge-ordering transition has a true structural component or consists merely of the reorganization of electrons. Neutrons probe the lattice directly, and we now show, based on neutron data, that the charge order is accompanied by a clear structural modification.
summary:
- Hidden charge order in Sr₃Fe₂O₇ emerges below ~330 K, confirmed by resonant X‑ray scattering.
- Neutron diffraction shows a clear lattice distortion accompanying the charge ordering.
- The charge disproportionation and localization transition, first noted in the 1960s, is now linked to a true structural change.

title: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries
abstract: arXiv:2611.22928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving quantum channels that are dualizable and pure. This provides an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries of quantum lattice systems, formulated in terms of their action on local operators. Focusing on quantum spin chains, we motivate these defining conditions and conjecture that every such quantum channel admits a realization by dualizable topological defects or, equivalently, by dualizable sequential quantum circuits. We construct a broad class of examples, including on-site non-invertible symmetries that are anomalous, as well as higher-dimensional examples. In Part II of this work, we reconstruct topological defects whose boundary algebras yield an index theory that classifies non-invertible QCAs up to blend equivalence.
summary:
- Defines non‑invertible QCAs as dualizable, pure, locality‑preserving quantum channels, giving an operator‑algebraic notion of non‑invertible lattice symmetries.

title: Competing Magnetic Orders and Continuously Varying Exponents in $U(1)$ Spin Liquids
abstract: arXiv:2611.23170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unequal couplings to a common emergent gauge field provide a continuous way to tune competing magnetic instabilities in an effective description of $U(1)$ spin-liquid mixtures. We study this mechanism in quantum electrodynamics in 2+1 dimensions with two families of four-component Dirac fermions. Combining a leading large-$N$ treatment with Schwinger--Dyson equations, we obtain chiral condensates representing N\'eel order in the two sectors. At fixed fermion number, the coupling ratio $\kappa=e_2^2/e_1^2$ controls which condensates develop. Depending on $N$, the phases with a single condensate are connected through either coexistence or a finite interval in which both fermion families remain gapless. The mass-generation thresholds are reciprocal, and the fermion gaps close with Miransky essential singularities. The renormalization group flow has a circular line of fixed points parametrized by the invariant ratio $\kappa$. At the calculated order, gauge-invariant staggered magnetization correlations have continuously varying exponents in the gapless regime, while the exponent for correlations between the two sectors is independent of $\kappa$. These results connect the competition between magnetic orders to a continuous family of critical theories and identify magnetic correlation signatures of the intervening gapless regime.
summary:
- Continuous tuning of competing Néel orders via unequal couplings to a shared U(gauge field in 2+1D QED with two Dirac families.
- Large‑N/Schwinger–Dyson analysis shows κ‑dependent chiral condensates, coexistence or a gapless interval, and Miransky‑type gap closing.
- RG flow yields a circular line of fixed points; staggered magnetization exponents vary continuously with κ, while inter‑sector correlations remain κ‑independent.
